title: Voter ID 2026: e-EPIC Download, ECINet App & Name Check
meta_description: Download e-EPIC free from voters.eci.gov.in or the ECINet app. Check your name after SIR deletions, register with Form 6, and fix details with Form 8.

hero.one_liner: Download your digital Voter ID free in minutes, and check that your name survived the electoral roll revision before the next election catches you out

sections.title: 📌 Check Your Name First: Crores Were Removed in the Roll Revision
sections.content:
The Special Intensive Revision has rewritten electoral rolls across India. In the phase covering 12 states and union territories, elector numbers fell from about 50.96 crore to 44.4 crore in the draft rolls, a removal of roughly 6.5 crore names.

Holding a Voter ID card does not mean your name is still on the roll. Deletions were recorded as deceased, shifted, duplicate, or forms not received, and plenty of living residents were caught in those buckets.

Search your name at electoralsearch.eci.gov.in before anything else on this page. Downloading the card is pointless if the roll no longer lists you.

sections.heading: What e-EPIC Is and Why It Beats the Plastic Card
content: e-EPIC is the Electronic Electoral Photo Identity Card, a secure PDF version of your Voter ID issued by the Election Commission. It carries your photo, name, EPIC number, constituency and a verifiable QR code.
It downloads instantly and free, while a physical card takes weeks to reach you by post. Both carry the same legal standing as identity proof.
The practical advantage is that it cannot be lost the way a plastic card can. Saved on your phone and in cloud storage, it survives a stolen wallet or a house move.
Anyone on the electoral roll can download it, regardless of whether the original registration was done online, through a BLO visit, or at the electoral registration office.
One caveat worth setting early: the e-EPIC reflects whatever the roll currently holds. If your details are wrong or your entry has been removed, downloading the card does not fix either problem.

sections.heading: Checking Whether You Are Still on the Roll

steps.title: Open electoralsearch.eci.gov.in
steps.desc: No login is needed. This is the public search against the currently published electoral roll.

steps.title: Search by EPIC number
steps.desc: The cleanest match. Enter the 10-character alphanumeric number printed on your card along with your state.

steps.title: Or search by details
steps.desc: Name with state, district and assembly constituency works when the card is missing. Expect namesakes in larger constituencies.

steps.title: Read the result carefully
steps.desc: Check the part number, serial number and polling station, not just that a name appeared. Polling stations were rationalised during the revision.

steps.title: If nothing comes up
steps.desc: You are not on the current roll. Fresh inclusion runs through Form 6, and your BLO can tell you why the name went.

sections.heading: What the SIR Actually Did to the Rolls
content: The Special Intensive Revision is a house-to-house verification of every entry, not the routine annual update. Booth Level Officers distributed enumeration forms and electors had to confirm their details within a fixed window.
Electors enrolled after 2003 were asked to establish name, date of birth and parents' details with documents. Those whose entry appeared in the 2003 roll faced a lighter requirement.
The scale of removal was unprecedented. West Bengal's draft dropped about 58 lakh names, and Uttar Pradesh retained 12.55 crore of its 15.44 crore electors.
The Supreme Court directed the Commission to publish deletion details openly, so state CEO websites carry lists of removed names with the stated reason.
Schedules run state by state and phases have continued through 2026. Check your own state's current SIR status on the ECI portal rather than assuming a national date applies to you.
If your household did receive a form and submitted it, keep the acknowledgement. Claims about non-receipt are far easier to contest when you can show what was filed and when.

sections.title: 🆕 The Voter Helpline App Is Now ECINet
sections.content:
ECI has folded more than 40 separate applications, including Voter Helpline, cVIGIL, Saksham and Know Your Candidate, into a single app called ECINet. It launched in January 2026 after being trialled during the Bihar assembly elections.

If you still have Voter Helpline installed, move to ECINet from the Play Store or App Store, or use ecinet.eci.gov.in. e-EPIC download, roll search, BLO contact and polling station lookup all live inside it now.

steps.title: Log in at voters.eci.gov.in
steps.desc: Register with your mobile number and OTP if it is your first visit. The same account handles every form later.

steps.title: Open the e-EPIC section
steps.desc: Choose download e-EPIC, then identify yourself by EPIC number or by the form reference number from a recent application.

steps.title: Verify by OTP
steps.desc: The OTP goes to the mobile number registered against your voter record, which is a common sticking point if that number has changed.

steps.title: Check details before downloading
steps.desc: Confirm name, relation name, age, address and constituency on screen. Anything wrong here needs Form 8 before the card is worth downloading.

steps.title: Download and back it up
steps.desc: Save the PDF to your phone and to cloud storage. If it asks for a password, it is normally your date of birth in DDMMYYYY format.

sections.heading: Three Ways to Get Your e-EPIC

win.name: VOTERS PORTAL
win.sub: voters.eci.gov.in handles download plus every form for corrections, shifting and new registration

others.name: ECINET APP
others.sub: Download, roll search, polling station and BLO contact in one app, with the card stored offline

others.name: DIGILOCKER
others.sub: Pull the card from the Election Commission as issuer and keep it beside Aadhaar and PAN with a verifiable QR

sections.heading: Reading Your EPIC Number and Card Details
content: The EPIC number is the 10-character alphanumeric code printed on your card, usually three letters followed by seven digits. It stays with you for life, even after corrections or a change of address.
It is the key to everything on the portal, so save it somewhere separate from the card itself. A photo of the card in cloud storage covers you if the physical one goes missing.

The card also lists your part number and serial number in the roll. Those two decide which polling station and which page of the register you appear on, which is what officials look up on polling day.

If your EPIC number appears on two records in different states, that is a duplicate entry and needs resolving through Form 7 for the old one. Duplicates were a major deletion category in the recent revision.
Note the part number down somewhere too. Polling staff locate you by part and serial far faster than by name, especially in a crowded booth on polling day.

sections.heading: 📋 Which Form You Actually Need
rows: For anyone not yet on the roll, including those deleted during revision who need fresh inclusion
For Indian citizens living abroad who hold an Indian passport
Voluntary submission of your Aadhaar number for roll authentication
To object to an entry, or to remove a name, for example after a death
Covers correction of entries, shifting of residence within or across constituencies, EPIC replacement, and PwD marking

sections.title: Form 8A No Longer Exists
sections.content:
Older guides still tell people to file Form 8A for shifting within a constituency, or Form 6 plus Form 7 for moving to a new constituency. Both instructions are out of date.

The Registration of Electors (Amendment) Rules came into force on 1 August 2022, discontinuing Form 8A and Form 001. Every shifting case, within or across constituencies, now goes through Form 8.

steps.title: Confirm you qualify
steps.description: You need Indian citizenship, ordinary residence in the constituency, and age 18 on or before the qualifying date. There are four qualifying dates a year: 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October.

steps.title: Fill Form 6 online
steps.description: Log in at voters.eci.gov.in and complete Form 6 with your name, date of birth, relation's name, address and contact details. The constituency is derived from your address.

steps.title: Upload proofs
steps.description: One age proof such as a birth certificate, class 10 marksheet or passport, one address proof such as Aadhaar, a utility bill, bank passbook or ration card, and a passport-size photograph.

steps.title: BLO verification
steps.description: The Booth Level Officer visits to confirm you live at the stated address. This usually takes a few weeks depending on the revision cycle.

steps.title: Collect your EPIC number
steps.description: Once included, your EPIC number is generated and notified by SMS. The e-EPIC becomes downloadable at that point.

sections.heading: Four Qualifying Dates: What Changed for Young Voters
content: Registration used to hang on a single annual cutoff of 1 January, which meant someone turning 18 in February waited nearly a year. The law now recognises four qualifying dates: 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October.
You qualify for the roll if you are 18 on or before the qualifying date you are applying against. Someone turning 18 in mid-March applies against the 1 April date.
Applications can be filed in advance of turning 18, so there is no reason to wait until the birthday itself. The system holds the application against the relevant date.

The practical effect is that a first-time voter rarely misses an election by a technicality now. What still catches people is applying too close to a poll, once the roll for that election has already been frozen.

sections.heading: If Your Name Was Deleted
content: Start by finding out why. State CEO websites publish deletion lists with the recorded reason, and your BLO can look up the entry against your old EPIC number.
Where the roll is still in its draft stage, the claims and objections window is the right route, and the correction happens before the final roll is published.
Where the final roll is already out, the route is fresh inclusion through Form 6 with your documents. Being previously registered does not restore you automatically.
Keep proof of everything you submit, including the acknowledgement number. Disputed deletions are easier to argue with a paper trail than with a recollection.
Do this well before an election rather than in the final week. Once the roll is frozen for a poll, no addition can help you vote in it.

sections.heading: Your BLO: The Person Who Can Actually Fix It
content: The Booth Level Officer maintains the roll for your polling area and is the single most useful contact for anything that has gone wrong with your entry.
They can tell you why a name was deleted, whether a form reached the office, and what document the verification is waiting on. That is information no portal screen shows you.
Find your BLO through the ECINet app or by calling 1950 with your part number. Most are local government staff or teachers working in your own area.
During revision drives they carry enumeration forms door to door. If nobody visited your household, that absence is worth flagging rather than assuming your entry is safe.
Keep any conversation factual and note the date. A record of who you spoke to and when helps if the matter escalates to the electoral registration officer.

sections.heading: Correcting Name, Address or Photo
content: Every correction now runs through Form 8 at voters.eci.gov.in, with proof of the correct detail uploaded. Your EPIC number does not change when details are corrected.
Name and date of birth mismatches against Aadhaar are the most common problem, and they matter beyond voting because banks compare documents.
For a change of address, Form 8 covers both a move within your constituency and a move to a different one. The old entry is removed as part of the same process.
An outdated photograph is worth replacing too, since polling officials match the face on the roll to the person at the booth.
Processing typically runs a few weeks, and status is trackable on the portal with the reference number from submission.
One correction at a time is the safer approach where several details are wrong, because a single rejected item can hold up the whole application.

sections.heading: Who Can and Cannot Register
qualify: Indian citizens aged 18 or above on the qualifying date
Ordinary residents of the constituency where they apply
NRIs holding an Indian passport, through Form 6A
Students living away from home, at either the hometown or the current address
disqualify: Anyone holding a foreign passport, including OCI and PIO card holders
People registered in more than one constituency, which is an offence
Persons disqualified under the law, such as by a court declaration of unsound mind
Those who cannot establish ordinary residence at the address claimed

sections.heading: Where the Voter ID Works as ID Proof
content: EPIC is widely accepted for bank KYC, SIM activation, passport applications and government scheme paperwork. It is one of the few documents that evidences citizenship as well as identity.
As address proof it is only as good as your last update. A card showing an address you left three years ago fails exactly when you need it.
As age proof it is weaker than it looks, because the date of birth was self-declared at registration. Government job and passport processes want a birth certificate or class 10 marksheet.
For the digital version, carrying a colour printout removes friction at institutions that have not adopted digital verification. It is the same document either way.
Keep in mind that no institution accepts a Voter ID as proof of citizenship for passport or government job purposes on its own. It supports the file, it does not close it.

sections.heading: Students, First-Time Voters and NRIs
content: Students living away can register either at the hometown address or at the current one, but not both. Choose the place you can realistically reach on polling day.
Campus enrolment drives run before qualifying dates in many universities, and a BLO processing your form in person is the fastest route available.
Turning 18 soon is not a reason to wait. With four qualifying dates a year, apply as the nearest one approaches rather than losing months.
NRIs register as overseas electors through Form 6A against the address in their Indian passport. Voting still requires being physically present at the polling station.
Overseas citizens who have taken foreign nationality, including OCI holders, cannot register at all. Indian citizenship is the requirement, not Indian origin.
Students who registered at a hostel address should remember to shift the entry after graduating. An entry left behind at a college address is exactly the profile revision drives mark as shifted.

items.title: Search the roll again
items.sub: Revisions change entries. Confirm your name, part number and polling station a few weeks before the poll.

items.title: Download a fresh e-EPIC
items.sub: Any correction you filed since the last download should be reflected on the card.

items.title: Locate the polling station
items.sub: Stations were rationalised during the revision, so last election's booth may not be yours now.

items.title: Keep a printout
items.sub: A colour print of the e-EPIC avoids arguments if a phone dies or a verifier hesitates.

items.title: Save 1950
items.sub: The national voter helpline handles roll queries, BLO contacts and complaints.

sections.title: The voter helpline number worth saving
sections.desc: It connects to your district election office for roll status, BLO details, polling station queries and complaints. Free from any phone across India.

SIR schedules and deletion lists are published state by state on Chief Electoral Officer websites. Check your own state's current position there.

sections.text: A Voter ID in your pocket proves nothing if the roll no longer has your name. Search first, download second.

sections.heading: Why the Download Fails and How to Fix It
content: The most common failure is an OTP that never arrives, because the mobile number on your voter record is one you no longer use. Update it through Form 8 and the download works afterwards.
An EPIC number entered with the wrong letters is the next most common. The letter block is easy to misread on a worn card, so cross-check it against the roll search result.
If the portal says no record found, your name may have been removed in the revision rather than the number being wrong. Search the roll before assuming a technical fault.
Pending applications also block the card. A correction or shifting request in progress means the e-EPIC becomes available only once the entry is finalised.
Where nothing resolves it, the helpline on 1950 routes you to your district election office, which can see the record status directly.
Finally, try the portal outside peak hours. Traffic spikes around revision deadlines and election announcements slow the servers noticeably.

faqs.question: How to download Voter ID card online?
faqs.answer:
Log in at voters.eci.gov.in with your mobile number and OTP, open the e-EPIC section, and identify yourself with your EPIC number or form reference number. Verify the details shown, then download the PDF.

The ECINet app and DigiLocker offer the same card. If the PDF asks for a password, it is usually your date of birth in DDMMYYYY format.

faqs.question: My name is missing from the voter list after SIR. What do I do?
faqs.answer:
First find the recorded reason. State CEO websites publish deletion lists, and your BLO can look up the old entry against your EPIC number.

If the roll is still in draft, use the claims and objections window. If the final roll is published, apply for fresh inclusion through Form 6 with age and address proof.

faqs.question: What is SIR and why were crores of names deleted?
faqs.answer:
The Special Intensive Revision is a house-to-house verification of every entry rather than the routine annual update, with electors enrolled after 2003 asked to document name, date of birth and parents' details.

In the phase covering 12 states and union territories, draft rolls fell from about 50.96 crore electors to 44.4 crore. Deletions were classified as deceased, shifted, duplicate, or forms not received.

faqs.question: Is the Voter Helpline app still working?
faqs.answer:
It has been migrated into ECINet, the Election Commission's single unified app launched in January 2026. ECINet absorbed more than 40 separate applications including Voter Helpline, cVIGIL and Know Your Candidate.

Install ECINet from the Play Store or App Store, or use ecinet.eci.gov.in. e-EPIC download and roll search work inside it.

faqs.question: I moved to a new city. How do I update my voter ID?
faqs.answer:
File Form 8 at voters.eci.gov.in and attach proof of the new address. Since the 2022 rules, Form 8 covers shifting both within your constituency and to a different one.

Ignore older advice about Form 8A or filing Form 6 plus Form 7 for a move. Form 8A was discontinued on 1 August 2022.

faqs.question: I lost my EPIC card. How do I get a duplicate?
faqs.answer:
Download the e-EPIC immediately from voters.eci.gov.in or ECINet, since it is legally equivalent and available at once.

For a replacement physical card, file Form 8 and select replacement of EPIC. Form 001 no longer exists for this purpose.

faqs.question: Is digital Voter ID valid at the polling booth?
faqs.answer:
The e-EPIC is issued by the Election Commission and serves as valid elector identity, whether shown on a phone or as a printout.

Carrying a colour printout is the practical choice, since it avoids any dispute with a verifier and does not depend on your battery.

faqs.question: Can I download Voter ID without an EPIC number?
faqs.answer:
Yes, if you have the form reference number from a recent application, or if your registered mobile number lets you log in and locate your record on the portal.

If you have neither, search electoralsearch.eci.gov.in by name, state, district and constituency to retrieve your EPIC number first.

faqs.question: What is the minimum age for voter registration?
faqs.answer:
You must be 18 on or before the qualifying date. There are four qualifying dates each year: 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October.

This means you no longer wait for a single annual cutoff. Apply as the nearest qualifying date approaches.

faqs.question: Can I have two voter IDs if I moved states?
faqs.answer:
No. Being registered in more than one constituency is an offence, and duplicate entries are exactly what revision drives remove.

Use Form 8 to shift your registration to the new address, which removes the old entry as part of the same process.

faqs.question: Can I register without Aadhaar?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Aadhaar linking through Form 6B is voluntary, and registration cannot be refused for not providing it.

Linking does help prevent duplicate entries and keeps your record consistent, but any accepted age and address proof is enough to register.

faqs.question: How long does new voter registration take?
faqs.answer:
Typically a few weeks from submission, covering BLO verification of your address and inclusion in the roll. Timelines stretch during intensive revision periods.

Track the application on voters.eci.gov.in with your reference number, and follow up with your BLO if verification has not happened.

faqs.question: Voter ID card kaise download kare?
faqs.answer:
voters.eci.gov.in par mobile number aur OTP se login karein, e-EPIC section kholen, aur apna EPIC number ya form reference number daalein. Details check karke PDF download kar lein, bilkul free.

Yahi card ECINet app aur DigiLocker par bhi milta hai. PDF password maange to aam taur par aapki date of birth DDMMYYYY format me hoti hai.

disclaimer: Voter registration processes and qualifying dates as per Election Commission of India (ECI) guidelines as of March 2026. Procedures may be updated - always check voters.eci.gov.in for latest information. Electoral roll updates follow ECI's official schedule.
